The group's research focuses on creating safe, data-efficient, and trustworthy robotic system intelligence. The group’s work encompasses several key areas: certified learning and control methods, the study of collective and swarm intelligence, and the use of geometric and physics-based models to enhance the adaptability of robotic systems. Furthermore, AIRoCS explores how robots can perceive and interact with their surroundings by integrating visual, tactile, and force sensors, as well as through human-robot interaction technologies like telepresence and immersive robotics.
 
The primary goal of the AIRoCS Group is to build intelligent robots capable of functioning autonomously, safely, and dependably in intricate, real-world settings. Name: Robotics Factory
Description:
Robots that energize the world.

Utility-scale solar farms are being built the same way they were 20 years ago — manually, slowly, and with significant quality variance. A 200MW site requires thousands of foundation piles, tens of thousands of tracker rails, and hundreds of thousands of module installations. Every one of them is placed by hand.

Robotics Factory is changing that.

We are building an autonomous robotic construction fleet — five specialised robots that own every phase of solar farm construction end-to-end: GPS-guided pile driving (±2mm accuracy), tracker and module installation at 3× human speed, cable trenching, and AI-powered digital twin quality assurance. Delivered as a per-watt subcontract service to EPC contractors across MENA and India.

No EPC buys robots. They buy megawatts delivered on time, on spec, at cost. That is what we sell.

We are currently raising our pre-seed round and actively building our founding technical team.
